question.text:
Paragraph: Electrical resistance of certain materials, known as superconductors, changes abruptly from a non-zero value to zero as their temperature is lowered below a critical temperature $T_C(0)$. An interesting property of superconductors is that their critical temperature becomes smaller than $T_C(0)$ if they are placed in a magnetic field i.e., the critical temperature $T_C(B)$ is a function of the magnetic field strength $B$. The dependence of $T_C(B)$ on $B$ is shown in the figure.
Question: In the graphs below, the resistance $R$ of a superconductor is shown as a function of its temperature $T$ for two different magnetic fields $B_1$ (solid line) and $B_2$ (dashed line). If $B_2$ is larger than $B_1$, which of the following graphs shows the correct variation of $R$ with $T$ in these fields?

solution.text:
If $B_2>B_1$, critical temperature, (at which resistance of semiconductors abruptly becomes zero) in case-2 will be less than compared to case- 1 .
$\therefore$ The correct option is (a).
